title: bug: submit_plan's rail refusal tells the planner to call propose_rail with targetScope "GLOBAL" | "EPIC" | "TASK", but checkPlanRails enforces only the global forbidden/required patterns, so an EPIC or TASK proposal can never lift a rail refusal (MCP_SERVER.md's Rail refusal note repeats the hint)
description:
Reported by architect-24611a0a from planning task-34e42a0a (msg-c788a9d9, 21:02Z on 2026-11-03). The governor re-checked it at tip ac3ea38f. The trap is live: that architect's own first submit_plan for 34e42a0a was refused because its test fixture quoted one of this board's forbiddenPatterns.

PROBLEM. A rail refusal's escape hatch offers all three scopes. EPIC and TASK proposals edit epicRails and taskRails, which the plan check never enforces. A planner who follows the hint with EPIC or TASK gets an approved proposal that changes nothing, and the plan stays refused.

EVIDENCE (at ac3ea38f):
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/submitPlan.ts:194-206 (assertPlanRails): `moe.propose_rail { proposalType: "ADD_RAIL" | "MODIFY_RAIL" | "REMOVE_RAIL", targetScope: "GLOBAL" | "EPIC" | "TASK", … }`.
- packages/moe-daemon/src/util/rails.ts:16-34 checks only `projectRails.forbiddenPatterns` and `projectRails.requiredPatterns`. The comment at :34 reads "Only forbiddenPatterns and global requiredPatterns are strictly enforced."
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md's submit_plan notes (about :378-380) say epicRails and taskRails are "NOT enforced in plan text". The Rail refusal bullet then says the message "goes on to name the moe.propose_rail escape hatch" without saying that only GLOBAL can lift it.

WHY BACKLOG, AFTER TWO ROWS.
- task-34e42a0a makes propose_rail able to reach the GLOBAL forbiddenPatterns and requiredPatterns at all. The new text must describe that landed path.
- task-2cc41d1a (amend_plan_step rails) may move assertPlanRails, and this refusal text with it, into util/rails.ts.
- The governor promotes this row when both are DONE.

FIX DIRECTION. The refusal names only targetScope "GLOBAL", with MODIFY_RAIL or REMOVE_RAIL of the exact forbiddenPatterns or requiredPatterns entry, in whatever shape 34e42a0a lands. The MCP_SERVER.md Rail refusal bullet says the same. Keep the refusal code and prefix (`-32003`, `Rail violation:`) unchanged.
definitionOfDone: The submit_plan rail refusal's escape-hatch text names only targetScope GLOBAL, together with the forbiddenPatterns or requiredPatterns entry shape that task-34e42a0a made reachable. A test pins that EPIC and TASK are not offered, and that the code -32003 and the 'Rail violation:' prefix are unchanged.

docs/MCP_SERVER.md's submit_plan Rail refusal note states that only a GLOBAL proposal can lift a rail refusal. The vitest run of the submit_plan and rails tests passes in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

The vitest output is large (logger INFO lines). Read only the `Test Files`, `Tests` and `FAIL` lines (mem:gotcha-propose-rail-global-lists).

Then run the RED gate once more. It must still print RED-AT-BASE, because it pins fa405c59's rails.ts. Quote its output in your completion summary.

Error handling for a red run:
- If an amendPlanStep or proposeRail test fails, re-run it in a second snapshot with HEAD's rails.ts overlaid.
- If it fails there too, it is pre-existing. Report it in #general and call moe.report_blocked with the evidence; do not edit those files.
- If it fails only with your change, fix rails.ts, never the test.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review (load adversarial-self-review) of your `git diff`. Fix any finding, then re-run step 3's gates.

(1) Scope: exactly 3 files.
- rails.ts: the message block and its comment.
- submitPlan.test.ts: the inserted lines only.
- MCP_SERVER.md: the one Rail refusal sentence.

(2) Nothing else moved:
- the code is still -32003 / CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION;
- the message still starts `[CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION] Rail violation: "<v>". Default action: <defaultAction>. `;
- error.data is still `{ tool, codeName }`;
- the MoeError context is unchanged.

(3) No EPIC, TASK or ADD_RAIL is offered anywhere in the message, for any violation. The architect's dry run printed the forbidden, required, odd-string and missing-violation shapes. The odd and missing shapes get the placeholder currentValue.

(4) currentValue is the exact entry:
- `rm -rf` for `Forbidden pattern: rm -rf`;
- `error handling` for `Required pattern missing: error handling`;
- a pattern that itself contains `: ` keeps everything after the FIRST label, because the regex anchors on the label.

(5) The amend_plan_step refusal shares the text. Its own default action is unchanged.

Follow-up, out of scope: the `Rail Proposals (escape hatch)` template in docs/roles/{architect,worker,governor}.reference.md still lists every scope for propose_rail in general (valid for editing guidance rails). Say in the completion summary that a refused plan needs GLOBAL MODIFY/REMOVE.

Then call moe.complete_task with step 3's evidence.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Name the scope only and leave currentValue generic. Rejected: quoting the exact entry, parsed from the violation's own label, makes the hatch copy-paste correct and avoids propose_rail's coded NOT_FOUND and ambiguity refusals. (2) Add a structured hatch to the MoeError context or suggestedAction. Rejected: the /ws and MCP boundary strips the context (error.data is { tool, codeName } only), so agents see only the message. (3) A new test block. Rejected in favour of extending the existing wire-level it.each, which already pins code, prefix and data across all three refusal paths. (4) Also fix the role reference docs' propose_rail template. Out of scope: the governor scoped this row to the Rail refusal note, and that template is a general propose_rail form.
